opportunities.title: Small Research Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers from all countries globally; projects can be conducted anywhere in the world. BES membership required. Not a scholarship; BES funding not for undergraduate/masters degrees or funded fellowships. PhD students have further eligibility criteria.
opportunities.summary: Provides funding up to £5,000 for new and innovative ecological research of the highest international standard, with a clear ecological science focus.

opportunities.title: Synthesis Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Main applicant must have BES membership; not required for all working group members. Groups of 8-15 individuals, diverse across institutions, career stages, genders and backgrounds, with international participation and EDI principles.
opportunities.summary: Fast-tracking innovative and impactful research by funding up to £30,000 towards the formation of new two-year synthesis groups that bring together diverse interdisciplinary groups to analyse existing data.

opportunities.title: Long-term Research Grants

amount.raw: £500 per year for a decade; £3,500 claimable in year 1 and an additional £3,500 in year 6 (up to £7,000 total)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership. Open to all types of ecologists including conservation practitioners, reserve managers and consultants, as well as university academics. Awarded to individuals, not organisations.
opportunities.summary: Provides a small amount of funding each year for 10 years to enable existing short-term projects with 1-2 years of data to be funded into the long term, funding projects such as ecological restoration, habitat creation, alien species control and climate change anywhere in the world.

opportunities.title: Pedagogical Research and Development Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership. No geographical restrictions; open to anyone involved in teaching ecology at any level, from early years to life-long learning in formal or informal settings. Awarded to individuals, not organisations. Projects max 12 months.
opportunities.summary: Improving the education of future generations of ecologists by providing up to £5,000 towards evidence-based learning, funding research on education methods within ecology to develop evidence informing teaching and learning practices.

opportunities.title: Connecting Ecologists with Other Disciplines Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership. Open to PhD students, postdoctoral fellows, early career ecologists, established researchers or employees of other organisations. Undergraduates and masters students not eligible. Awarded to individuals; placements up to 12 months.
opportunities.summary: Promoting interdisciplinary skills by funding up to £20,000 towards placements in different disciplines and sectors, allowing an ecologist to immerse in another professional world (another discipline, NGO, public sector, business) for up to 12 months.

opportunities.title: Outreach and Engagement Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Lead applicant must have BES membership. Open to individuals, teams and organisations across all experience levels to organise ecological public engagement events. Projects max 12 months. No restrictions on where applicants come from or carry out work.
opportunities.summary: Provides funding up to £2,000 for individuals, teams and organisations to engage public audiences with the excitement, importance and relevance of ecological science, in diverse formats including in-person events, digital formats or physical resources.

opportunities.title: Training and Travel Grants

amount.raw: maximum of £250 for virtual conferences/courses, maximum of £500 for in-person events

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must be a BES member and a PhD student or postgraduate researcher (postdocs, undergraduates and masters students not eligible). Must work/study at a university or research institution providing research facilities, in areas within the science of ecology.
opportunities.summary: Helps PhD students and postgraduate researchers meet the costs of specialist field training courses, and network and publicise their research by presenting their work at workshops and conferences. Awarded on a lottery-based system. Next round opens 24 August 2026.

opportunities.title: Annual Meeting Grants 2026
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must be a BES member at any research career stage; must be a citizen of and based in the Global South, travelling from and returning to that country; must have applied to present at the Annual Meeting; at least three years since last BES Training and Travel Grant.
opportunities.summary: Supports researchers based in Global South countries to attend the BES Annual Meeting 2026 in the UK, covering costs directly related to attending such as registration, transport, food and accommodation. Awarded via lottery. Open 17 July - 8 September 2026.
